Rep. Miller nails it—rural healthcare is collapsing under bureaucratic red tape. H.R.3421’s Section 611 global budgets for institutional providers will strangle rural hospitals with administrative overhead, not fix chronic disease care. D.C. elites push single-payer scams while ignoring rural clinics’ pleas for basic resources. Cut the NIH’s bloated research slush funds and redirect to rural telemedicine and early detection programs. Taxpayers deserve real solutions, not another government-run healthcare disaster.

EMS saving lives on the frontlines deserve every resource—but Washington’s track record on healthcare spending is abysmal. The CARE Act’s heart is in the right place, but without strict audits and accountability, it risks becoming another bureaucratic slush fund. 

Look at H.R. 9706’s homelessness report—$1.39 trillion in DOD spending while medical programs get scraps. Prioritize EMS funding by cutting waste elsewhere, not adding to the debt. 

Every dollar should go to heroes in the field, not middlemen in suits.

The RESILIENCE Act is textbook D.C. theater—pretending to fix problems they created. The Inflation Reduction Act rigged the game with corporate handouts, then this bill tries to bandage utility taxes while leaving the same bloated bureaucracy intact.

Deducting repair costs? Fine. But letting utilities write off expenses under AMT without slashing the underlying regulatory bloat is like rearranging deck chairs on the Titanic. Miller’s “bipartisan” push ignores the root issue: government shouldn’t be picking energy winners or complicating tax codes.

Real reform means gutting the AMT entirely, not tweaking deductions. Until then, it’s just more accounting gimmicks masking systemic waste.
